prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher (sets permitted export) when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands/output target within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System (within envelope, no protection override), Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (within ratings), Nacelle Condition Monitor (stress review)→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer (loading/temp, escalate), export cable, Export Cable Monitor (temp/loading/alarms), station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates, notifies Grid Dispatcher, reports limitations; acts only after state check and Control Engineer authorization; reports each step. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped generation/export/status→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. SCADA Engineer: investigates telemetry gaps. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment. Grid Dispatcher: targets, restrictions; priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag; coordinated output adjustment. Mode Grid Constraint (restriction from grid instruction/cable/substation limit, until clarified/withdrawn): Duty Planner records revised basis, gets authorization; Control Engineer verifies level/effective time/ramp, reduces power stepwise, compares export, escalates threats; no chasing in-tolerance fluctuations. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale, work/constraint impact. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; switching sequence with Control Engineer (one action/step, hold points); records; restoration after Field Supervisor confirms clear. Ambiguity/failure: pause, safe state. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet.

New part:
S561: The Duty Planner maintains a clear record of the restriction, response actions, approvals, and outstanding checks for shift handover.
S562: When the restriction is released, the Control Engineer confirms authorization and restores output gradually while monitoring equipment response.
S563: This section defines how personnel counts are reconciled during marine operations and how discrepancies are escalated.
S564: Reconciliation applies to each movement between shore, a vessel, and an offshore work location.
S565: The Marine Coordinator establishes the expected personnel count and destination for each movement before transfer begins.
S566: Counts are maintained separately for each vessel and each work location to avoid combining unrelated movements.
S567: The Vessel Master verifies the number of people physically aboard before departure.
S568: The Crew Transfer Vessel and Daughter Craft are accounted for independently when they operate in the same transfer sequence.
S569: The North Access Scanner records personnel access events at the north access point.
S570: The South Access Scanner records personnel access events at the south access point.
S571: The Personnel Tracking Console maintains the operational count for active marine movements.
S572: Personnel are checked against the expected count at departure, arrival, and any intermediate transfer point.
S573: The count correction is used by the Personnel Tracking Console to update a verified personnel total.
S574: A corrected total is accepted only after the reason for the discrepancy has been established and recorded.
S575: Any difference between the expected and observed count remains unresolved until every person is accounted for.
S576: The Marine Coordinator pauses further personnel transfers when a discrepancy is identified.
S577: The Vessel Master maintains a safe operating position while the discrepancy is investigated.
S578: The Marine Coordinator informs the Shore Control Room of the discrepancy and the immediate control actions.
S579: The HSE Officer assesses any safety implications and advises whether the affected activity can continue.
S580: If a person's location is uncertain, the Rescue Coordinator is notified without delay.
S581: A discrepancy involving a transfer to an offshore work location is checked against the arrival count before work proceeds.
S582: A discrepancy involving a return movement is checked before the vessel departs the work location.
S583: The Marine Coordinator escalates any unresolved discrepancy to the Duty Planner and records the time of escalation.
S584: The record includes the expected count, observed count, persons still unaccounted for, actions taken, and current status.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
